patch_description: The current Kalman filter achieves excellent lag error (0.18) and correlation (0.91), but suffers from high slope_changes (317.2) and false_reversals (253.6) — the causal filter tracks noise-induced micro-oscillations too closely. Following the recommendation, I add a final lightweight zero-phase post-processing stage: compute the gradient of the Kalman output, flag short segments where the sign of the gradient flips while the gradient magnitude is small relative to the median (residual micro-oscillations), and apply an extra short zero-phase Savitzky-Golay pass only in a dilated neighborhood of those flagged regions. Since smoothing is restricted to flagged neighborhoods, the well-performing lag/correlation characteristics remain intact elsewhere, while spurious directional reversals are suppressed. This directly targets slope_changes and false_reversals — the two weakest metrics — without sacrificing the responsiveness advantage over the previous zero-phase-heavy program (which had 0.29 lag but only scored 0.59).
